name: Cervical Radiculopathy
summary: Cervical nerve-root disorder causing neck/arm pain with sensory, motor or reflex changes in a root distribution.
firstSteps: Education and position/activity modification
Repeated or directional movement when clearly beneficial
Gentle neural mobility
aka: pinched nerve in neck arm pain from neck cervical disc nerve root

name: Mechanical Neck Pain
summary: Neck pain associated with movement, posture or sustained loading, without evidence that a specific serious pathology or nerve-root disorder explains the presentation.
redFlags: Fever, immunosuppression, cancer history or unexplained weight loss
Progressive neurological deficit, gait disturbance, hand clumsiness or bowel/bladder change
firstSteps: Explain the generally favourable course and encourage comfortable daily activity
Use relative load modification rather than immobilisation
Gentle active cervical and thoracic movement; short frequent movement breaks
aka: neck pain stiff neck text neck cervical spondylosis cervical pain

name: Temporomandibular Disorder (TMD)
summary: Education, jaw exercise, habit modification and selected manual therapy can improve pain and function in musculoskeletal TMD.
firstSteps: Measure comfortable mouth opening and pain with chewing/yawning.
Assess deviation, joint sounds, masticatory tenderness and cervical function.
Identify clenching or high-load habits.
aka: TMJ TMD jaw pain jaw clicking lockjaw

name: Whiplash-Associated Disorder (WAD)
summary: Neck symptoms following acceleration–deceleration trauma, commonly a road traffic collision; classify severity and screen carefully for associated injury.
redFlags: Midline tenderness or high-risk trauma requiring Canadian C-Spine Rule assessment
Loss of consciousness, severe headache or repeated vomiting
Progressive weakness, sensory loss, gait change
firstSteps: Exclude serious injury and classify WAD grade
Provide reassurance, clear information and encouragement to resume ordinary activity as tolerated
Use gentle active movement and avoid unnecessary immobilisation
aka: whiplash neck injury car accident neck

name: Acromioclavicular (AC) Joint Injury
summary: Injury to the AC and, in higher grades, coracoclavicular ligaments, commonly after a fall onto the shoulder.
firstSteps: Protect from painful compression and heavy lifting
Use sling briefly only if needed for comfort and clinician-directed
Maintain elbow, wrist and hand movement; begin shoulder ROM as tolerated
aka: AC joint separated shoulder AC sprain

name: Adhesive Capsulitis (Frozen Shoulder)
summary: Painful progressive restriction of active and passive glenohumeral movement, typically with external rotation most limited.
redFlags: Acute traumatic inability to elevate arm
Fever, hot swollen joint or systemic illness
Cancer history, unexplained mass or constitutional symptoms
firstSteps: Education about variable natural history and symptom-guided activity
Maintain tolerable movement; avoid forceful stretching during highly irritable phase
Coordinate medical management of pain and relevant metabolic conditions
aka: frozen shoulder stiff shoulder shoulder freezing capsulitis

name: Anterior Shoulder Instability
summary: Recurrent or traumatic tendency of the humeral head to translate anteriorly, often after dislocation or subluxation.
firstSteps: Protect vulnerable abduction/ER range early
Pain-free ROM
Isometric cuff activation
aka: dislocated shoulder shoulder dislocation shoulder subluxation Bankart

name: Full-Thickness Rotator Cuff Tear
summary: Complete disruption through the tendon thickness, ranging from degenerative tears with preserved function to acute traumatic tears with major weakness.
redFlags: Acute traumatic inability to elevate arm
firstSteps: Orthopaedic referral for acute traumatic full-thickness tears, pseudoparalysis or major functional loss
Discuss goals, age, tendon quality, tear size and functional demand
aka: rotator cuff tear shoulder tear torn cuff

name: Long-Head Biceps Tendinopathy
summary: Anterior shoulder pain associated with loading of the long-head biceps tendon; frequently coexists with rotator cuff or labral pathology.
redFlags: Acute traumatic loss of strength or suspected rupture
Marked deformity/Popeye sign with acute pain
firstSteps: Modify painful overhead and heavy supination loads
Maintain comfortable shoulder ROM
Explain tendon load management and avoid complete rest
aka: biceps tendinitis biceps tendon pain front of shoulder

name: Rotator Cuff Tendinopathy / Subacromial Pain
summary: Load-related rotator cuff pain, often aggravated by elevation and overhead activity; modern management emphasizes active rehabilitation rather than a purely mechanical 'impingement' model.
firstSteps: Education and temporary modification of provocative overhead volume
Begin cuff/scapular motor-control work
Maintain comfortable ROM
aka: rotator cuff impingement subacromial pain painful arc shoulder pain overhead

name: Carpal Tunnel Syndrome
summary: Median nerve compression at the carpal tunnel causing nocturnal paresthesia, sensory symptoms and sometimes thenar weakness.
firstSteps: Neutral wrist night splint when appropriate
Activity/ergonomic modification
Education about symptom-provoking wrist positions
aka: CTS median nerve tingling fingers numb hands at night

name: De Quervain Tenosynovitis
summary: Painful disorder of the first dorsal extensor compartment involving abductor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis brevis tendons.
redFlags: Sudden tendon dysfunction or neurological deficit
firstSteps: Modify repetitive painful thumb/wrist tasks
Consider thumb-spica support for short-term symptom control
Maintain comfortable finger and wrist motion
aka: mother's wrist thumb tendon pain texting thumb wrist thumb side pain

name: Lateral Epicondylalgia (Tennis Elbow)
summary: Load-related lateral elbow pain involving the common wrist-extensor tendon, especially extensor carpi radialis brevis.
firstSteps: Modify gripping/lifting volume
Begin pain-monitored isometric or isotonic wrist extensor loading
aka: tennis elbow lateral epicondylitis outer elbow pain

name: Medial Epicondylalgia (Golfer's Elbow)
summary: Load-related pain at the common flexor-pronator tendon origin, aggravated by gripping, wrist flexion or forearm pronation.
redFlags: Progressive ulnar nerve weakness or persistent sensory loss
Hot swollen joint, fever or fracture concern
firstSteps: Temporarily reduce high-irritability gripping and throwing volume
Maintain pain-tolerable elbow/wrist movement
Explain graded tendon loading
aka: golfer's elbow medial epicondylitis inner elbow pain

name: Trigger Finger (Stenosing Flexor Tenosynovitis)
summary: A flexor tendon gliding disorder at the A1 pulley causing painful clicking, catching or locking during finger flexion and extension.
redFlags: Hot swollen digit with fever or suspected infection
Fixed deformity or rapidly progressive dysfunction
firstSteps: Reduce repeated forceful gripping temporarily
Maintain comfortable tendon glide and full finger extension where possible
Consider night splinting in selected early cases
aka: stenosing tenosynovitis finger locking finger catching

name: Axial Spondyloarthritis / Ankylosing Spondylitis
summary: Regular exercise, mobility, posture, aerobic fitness and strength are central alongside rheumatology medical management.
redFlags: New neurological symptoms after even minor trauma
firstSteps: Measure spinal mobility, posture, chest expansion, hip/shoulder ROM and function.
Ask about eye symptoms, fracture history and neurological change.
Build a daily mobility routine.
aka: AS axial spondyloarthritis inflammatory back pain bamboo spine

name: Lumbar Radiculopathy
summary: Lumbar nerve-root disorder causing radiating leg pain with possible sensory, motor or reflex changes; distinguish radicular pain from radiculopathy with objective deficit.
firstSteps: Screen neurological status and red flags; document baseline strength
Provide education and maintain tolerable activity
Find positions and movements that permit function without repeatedly provoking distal symptoms
aka: sciatica slipped disc disc herniation prolapse sciatic nerve leg pain from back radiating leg pain

name: Non-Specific Low Back Pain
summary: Low back pain for which no specific serious structural cause is identified; management focuses on function, education and progressive activity.
redFlags: New urinary retention/incontinence, saddle sensory loss or bilateral progressive weakness
Fever, immunosuppression, cancer history or unexplained weight loss
Significant trauma, fracture risk or prolonged steroid use
firstSteps: Explain the common non-specific nature and favourable prognosis for many episodes
Encourage continued daily activity and avoid bed rest
Use comfortable movement and short walking bouts
aka: low back pain backache lumbago kamar dard nonspecific LBP mechanical back pain

name: Thoracic Spine Pain
summary: Pain in the thoracic region that may be mechanical but warrants careful screening because cardiopulmonary, visceral, fracture and systemic causes can mimic musculoskeletal pain.
redFlags: Chest pressure, breathlessness, sweating or exertional symptoms
Fever, cancer history, unexplained weight loss
firstSteps: Screen urgent causes before musculoskeletal treatment
Maintain comfortable walking and thoracic movement when safe
Modify aggravating load temporarily without prolonged rest
aka: mid back pain upper back pain thoracic pain between shoulder blades

name: Adductor-Related Groin Pain
summary: Groin pain associated with the adductor muscle-tendon complex, often provoked by resisted adduction and palpation near the adductor origin.
redFlags: Acute testicular pain/swelling or abdominal emergency
firstSteps: Reduce painful sprinting, kicking and cutting load
Maintain pain-tolerable walking and hip ROM
Begin low-load adductor isometrics
aka: groin strain adductor strain groin pain footballer

name: Femoroacetabular Impingement Syndrome (FAIS)
summary: Symptomatic nonarthritic hip condition involving motion-related hip/groin pain with clinical findings and cam/pincer morphology when imaging is relevant.
firstSteps: Modify deep flexion/adduction/IR exposure
Hip and trunk mobility where truly restricted
Begin hip/trunk strengthening
aka: FAI hip impingement cam pincer groin pain hip

name: Gluteal Tendinopathy
summary: Load-related gluteus medius/minimus tendon pain, usually presenting as lateral hip pain and often overlapping with GTPS.
redFlags: Acute trauma with inability to bear weight
Systemic illness, fever or unexplained weight loss
firstSteps: Reduce compressive positions and excessive adduction
Modify running/stair load
Begin tolerable isometric abductor loading
aka: gluteal tendon pain buttock tendon side hip lying pain

name: Greater Trochanteric Pain Syndrome (GTPS)
summary: Lateral hip pain commonly associated with gluteal tendon pathology and compression sensitivity around the greater trochanter; isolated bursitis is an oversimplification.
redFlags: Inability to weight bear after trauma
Cancer history, unexplained weight loss or severe night pain
firstSteps: Reduce sustained hip adduction/compressive positions; modify side-lying with pillow support
Adjust walking/running load temporarily
Begin tolerable isometric abductor work
aka: GTPS trochanteric bursitis side of hip pain lateral hip pain

name: Hamstring Strain
summary: Musculotendinous hamstring injury commonly occurring during high-speed running or excessive lengthening.
firstSteps: Avoid high-strain stretching/sprinting initially
Begin symptom-guided low-load contractions
Maintain hip/trunk and contralateral conditioning
aka: pulled hamstring hamstring tear back of thigh pain sprinter

name: Hip Osteoarthritis
summary: Hip OA commonly causes groin/anterior thigh pain, mobility loss and reduced walking function; rehabilitation emphasizes exercise, education and selected manual therapy.
firstSteps: Education
Activity pacing
Hip mobility within tolerance
aka: hip arthritis hip OA hip replacement hip wear

name: ACL Reconstruction Rehabilitation
summary: Criterion-based rehabilitation restores extension, quadriceps strength, movement quality, running and sport capacity while respecting surgical and graft-specific precautions.
redFlags: Possible DVT: new calf swelling/pain, warmth or unexplained shortness of breath; urgent medical assessment is required, with emergency response for chest pain or breathing difficulty
Possible infection: fever, increasing wound redness, drainage or rapidly worsening pain/swelling
Locked knee, sudden major extension loss or acute instability event
firstSteps: Review operative note, graft and restrictions.
Check wound, effusion, extension, flexion, quadriceps activation, gait and DVT warning signs.
Start extension restoration and quadriceps activation immediately if permitted.
aka: ACL surgery ACL reconstruction rehab after ACL operation graft

name: Anterior Cruciate Ligament (ACL) Injury
summary: Partial or complete ACL disruption causing rotational and anterior knee instability, often during pivoting, deceleration or awkward landing.
redFlags: Locked knee suggesting displaced meniscal tear
firstSteps: Education and activity modification
Restore full extension early
Progress flexion
aka: ACL tear anterior cruciate ligament cruciate knee giving way

name: Knee Osteoarthritis
summary: Clinical osteoarthritis causing activity-related knee pain, stiffness and functional limitation; exercise and education are core treatments.
redFlags: Hot swollen joint with systemic illness
firstSteps: Explain OA as manageable and not simply irreversible wear
Tailor activity
Discuss weight management when appropriate
aka: knee arthritis knee OA knee wear and tear knee replacement ghutne ka dard

name: Medial Collateral Ligament (MCL) Injury
summary: Valgus-related injury of the medial knee ligament complex, often managed non-operatively when isolated.
firstSteps: Protect from valgus stress and control swelling
Use brace/crutches if needed based on severity
Restore extension, flexion and quadriceps activation
aka: MCL sprain medial collateral ligament inner knee ligament

name: Meniscal Injury
summary: Traumatic or degenerative injury of the medial or lateral meniscus, presenting with joint-line pain, swelling and sometimes catching or locking.
firstSteps: Relative load modification
ROM restoration
Quadriceps activation
aka: meniscus tear cartilage tear knee locking torn cartilage

name: Patellar Tendinopathy
summary: Load-related pain at the patellar tendon, commonly at the inferior pole, in jumping and running athletes.
redFlags: Acute pop with extensor mechanism failure
Inability to actively extend knee or perform straight-leg raise
Large traumatic effusion or suspected fracture
firstSteps: Reduce jump/sprint volume to tolerable level
Maintain strength with isometrics or reduced-range resistance
Explain that complete rest often reduces capacity
aka: jumper's knee patellar tendonitis patellar tendon pain

name: Patellofemoral Pain
summary: Peripatellar or retropatellar pain aggravated by loaded knee flexion such as stairs, squatting, running or prolonged sitting.
redFlags: Large acute effusion or traumatic onset
firstSteps: Explain load-capacity relationship and adjust painful running/jumping temporarily
Continue tolerable activity
Begin knee and/or hip strengthening at manageable range
aka: runner's knee kneecap pain anterior knee pain PFPS chondromalacia

name: Posterior Cruciate Ligament (PCL) Injury
summary: Partial or complete PCL injury causing posterior tibial laxity, commonly after a dashboard injury or fall onto a flexed knee.
firstSteps: Protect knee and control effusion
Avoid posterior tibial sag and hamstring loading early when prescribed
Restore ROM and quadriceps activation
aka: PCL tear posterior cruciate ligament dashboard injury

name: Achilles Tendinopathy
summary: Load-related pain and impaired function in the midportion or insertional Achilles tendon, commonly aggravated by running and hopping.
redFlags: Sudden pop and loss of plantar-flexion function (rupture)
firstSteps: Adjust running/jumping load while maintaining tolerable activity
Begin calf isometrics or controlled raises
For insertional symptoms, initially limit deep dorsiflexion compression
aka: Achilles tendonitis Achilles pain heel cord pain

name: Achilles Tendon Rupture
summary: Partial or complete rupture of the Achilles tendon, commonly presenting with sudden posterior-ankle pain and loss of plantar-flexion function.
redFlags: Suspected rupture requires prompt medical/orthopaedic pathway
firstSteps: Prompt orthopaedic/medical assessment
Immobilize in plantar flexion/equinus according to local protocol
Avoid unprotected dorsiflexion stretching
aka: Achilles tear snapped Achilles ruptured tendon heel cord

name: Lateral Ankle Sprain
summary: Injury of the lateral ankle ligament complex, most commonly the ATFL, often after inversion with plantar flexion.
redFlags: Ottawa Ankle Rules indication for radiography
firstSteps: External support with brace or taping based on severity
Progressive weight bearing as tolerated
Compression/elevation for swelling
aka: ankle sprain twisted ankle rolled ankle inversion sprain

name: Plantar Heel Pain (Plantar Fasciopathy)
summary: Load-related plantar-medial heel pain, often worst with first steps after rest; the term fasciopathy better reflects many persistent cases.
redFlags: Night/rest pain, systemic symptoms or malignancy history
firstSteps: Modify sudden walking/running load
Use supportive footwear and temporary taping/heel support if helpful
Begin plantar fascia-specific and calf stretching if tolerated
aka: plantar fasciitis heel pain heel spur policeman's heel

name: Posterior Tibial Tendon Dysfunction (Progressive Collapsing Foot Deformity)
summary: A spectrum of medial ankle tendon pain and progressive foot deformity associated with posterior tibial tendon and supporting ligament insufficiency.
redFlags: Hot swollen foot or neuropathic diabetic foot concern
firstSteps: Reduce aggravating walking load and provide supportive footwear/orthosis when appropriate
Begin tolerable inversion and calf activation
Assess diabetes, neuropathy and skin integrity
aka: PTTD flat foot adult acquired flatfoot tibialis posterior

name: Tibial Bone Stress Injury
summary: Load-related tibial bone stress continuum from periosteal reaction to stress fracture, often associated with abrupt increases in running or impact.
redFlags: Pain at rest/night or inability to bear weight
Anterior tibial cortex focal pain (higher-risk site)
firstSteps: Stop running/jumping that provokes bone pain
Maintain pain-free cross-training only if medically appropriate
Assess footwear, training error, nutrition and bone-health risk
aka: shin splints medial tibial stress syndrome stress fracture shin pain

name: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)
summary: Canalith repositioning is the primary treatment after confirming the affected canal and excluding central or vascular warning signs.
redFlags: Continuous spontaneous vertigo with central signs
firstSteps: Take a detailed vertigo history: duration, triggers and associated neurological symptoms.
Perform oculomotor/neurological screening if presentation is not classic.
Use Dix-Hallpike or supine roll testing as appropriate.
aka: BPPV vertigo dizziness benign positional vertigo Epley spinning

name: Cerebral Palsy
summary: Goal-directed, family-centered rehabilitation focuses on participation, strength, mobility, motor learning, positioning and assistive technology rather than passive correction alone.
firstSteps: Clarify child/family goals.
Assess GMFCS level, mobility, strength, ROM, selective motor control and equipment.
Choose functional play tasks that directly match goals.
aka: CP spastic child cerebral palsy children

name: Parkinson's Disease
summary: Large-amplitude movement, cueing, strength, balance, gait and aerobic exercise help preserve function and manage bradykinesia and falls risk.
firstSteps: Assess gait speed, turning, freezing triggers, balance, falls and dual-task difficulty.
Check orthostatic symptoms and fatigue.
Teach one amplitude strategy and one cueing strategy.
aka: Parkinson tremor shuffling gait PD

name: Spinal Cord Injury Rehabilitation
summary: Rehabilitation is level- and completeness-specific, emphasizing prevention of secondary complications, strength, mobility, transfers, wheelchair skills, standing/gait when appropriate and lifelong health.
firstSteps: Review neurological level/completeness and medical precautions.
Check respiratory status, skin, ROM, spasticity, transfers and wheelchair needs.
Screen autonomic dysreflexia risk in lesions where relevant.
aka: SCI paraplegia quadriplegia tetraplegia spinal injury

name: Stroke Rehabilitation
summary: High-repetition, task-specific practice, strength, aerobic activity and functional training are central, with safety and individual neurological deficits guiding dosage.
redFlags: New neurological deterioration suggesting recurrent stroke
Acute DVT or severe medical instability
firstSteps: Assess transfers, sitting/standing balance, walking, upper-limb function, sensation, neglect and communication needs.
Check blood pressure, heart rate and medical stability.
Choose one mobility goal and one upper-limb/ADL goal.
aka: stroke CVA hemiplegia hemiparesis brain attack after stroke

name: COPD Pulmonary Rehabilitation
summary: Exercise training, breathing strategies, education and self-management form the core of pulmonary rehabilitation, with oxygen and medical therapies coordinated with the treating team.
redFlags: Severe resting hypoxemia outside prescribed parameters
firstSteps: Record dyspnea, SpO2, heart rate, 6MWT/sit-to-stand and exacerbation history.
Review oxygen prescription and medical restrictions.
Teach pacing and breathing control during exertion.
aka: COPD chronic obstructive pulmonary disease emphysema chronic bronchitis breathlessness lung rehab

name: Post-CABG Cardiac Rehabilitation
summary: Early mobilization and structured cardiac rehabilitation restore aerobic capacity, strength and confidence while respecting sternotomy and medical precautions.
firstSteps: Check heart rate, BP, SpO2, rhythm concerns, wound and sternal status.
Assess bed mobility, transfers and walking.
Teach supported cough/breathing if needed and begin safe walking.
aka: heart surgery bypass surgery CABG open heart cardiac rehab

name: Fibromyalgia
summary: Graded exercise, education, sleep and pacing strategies are central. Manual therapy may offer temporary comfort but should not reinforce beliefs of tissue damage or fragility.
redFlags: Inflammatory/systemic features inconsistent with known diagnosis
Unexplained major weight loss or fever
firstSteps: Assess widespread pain, fatigue, sleep, current activity and the patient's biggest functional limitation.
Start below the patient's flare threshold.
Choose an enjoyable form of aerobic activity plus simple strength.
aka: widespread pain chronic pain fatigue tender points

name: Post-Mastectomy Rehabilitation
summary: Rehabilitation addresses shoulder mobility, strength, scar symptoms, posture, lymphedema risk and return to daily activity while coordinating with oncology care.
redFlags: New unilateral swelling suggesting DVT or acute lymphedema complication
firstSteps: Check wound status, shoulder ROM, pain, swelling and sensory symptoms.
Measure arm circumference/volume when lymphedema concern exists.
Begin gentle shoulder mobility and breathing.
aka: breast surgery mastectomy lymphedema shoulder after breast cancer surgery
